clinician.trajectory_summary: A 40-year-old woman presented with one month of abdominal pain and several episodes of non-projectile vomiting. Physical examination revealed epigastric and right hypochondriac tenderness with hepatomegaly. Abdominal ultrasound with Doppler demonstrated heterogeneous liver echotexture, a fibrous cord replacing the middle hepatic vein, absence of color flow in hepatic veins, and mild ascites. Contrast-enhanced CT confirmed complete thrombosis of the middle and left hepatic veins with partial thrombosis of the right hepatic vein, slit-like visualization of the hepatic IVC, caudate lobe enlargement, and nutmeg liver appearance. Diagnostic hepatic vein venography was performed and confirmed the imaging findings. These findings are diagnostic of Budd-Chiari syndrome (hepatic vein thrombosis).
